analyst.summary: Anand Rathi Wealth's Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) print is a clean beat on the franchise metrics that matter: AUM crossed Rs 1,06,300 crore (+21% YoY, Rs 2,743 crore net inflows), RM productivity rose (AUM/RM Rs 249 crore vs Rs 224 crore YoY) even as headcount grew, and client/RM attrition remain near-zero (0.09% client attrition, zero regret RM attrition). Revenue mix stays 57% structured-products (MLD) versus 43% MF-distribution/brokerage -- a differentiator that already survived the 2023 MLD tax-arbitrage removal but keeps the business concentrated in one regulation-sensitive product line -- and Q1 FY27 showed the first real margin crack, EBITDA margin down ~1,289bps YoY to ~33.7%, attributed by management to RM-hiring investment. At a market cap of ~Rs 34,600-34,900 crore against trailing PAT of ~Rs 400-410 crore, the stock trades near 85-90x earnings (consistent with the quant snapshot's 87.3x), a PEG of roughly 3x against its own 3-year growth and over 5x against its own FY27 guidance (PAT +16-19% to Rs 460 crore, a clear deceleration from FY26). Recent SEBI penalties in the news belong to the group's separate broking arm (ARSSBL), not this listed entity. Recommendation: Sell -- on valuation, not on any asset-quality or governance flag on ANANDRATHI itself; this is a genuine, close judgment call on an otherwise pristine franchise.
